name: open-jtalk
why: Text to Japanese speech built from HMM synthesis gives a rare look at how speech is modelled and generated.

brief.what_it_is: Open JTalk is a Japanese text-to-speech system: it takes Japanese text and produces synthesized Japanese speech. The homepage describes it only in those terms and does not spell out inputs or outputs further. Two executables are listed for the Homebrew formula, hts_engine and open_jtalk. The system needs a Japanese dictionary and a separate HTS voice file to run.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no motivation beyond the one-line description that it is a Japanese text-to-speech system. The scout note says it offers a rare look at how speech is modelled and generated, which is the scout's framing rather than the author's.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the synthesis mechanism. It links to HTK, HTS, SPTK, hts_engine API, MeCab and the NAIST Japanese Dictionary, and the HTS voice is described as trained on the Nitech Japanese Speech Database. The scout note says it is built from HMM synthesis, but the homepage itself does not confirm that.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage says you can compile the dictionary yourself, or use one of three precompiled binary dictionary packages: Shift-JIS, EUC-JP or UTF-8. Version 1.11 of the dictionary is dated 25 December 2018. A voice is a separate download: HTS voice version 1.05 (25 December 2012), as a binary package. The page says it works on Linux machines and does not mention macOS. No commands or configuration steps are shown on the homepage.
brief.standout: The Japanese-only, open-source, statistical-parametric approach stands out: the stack is built from HTK, HTS and SPTK, with MeCab handling the text analysis. The voice is trained on a named public speech database, so the model can be inspected rather than treated as a black box.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest Open JTalk release on the homepage is version 1.11 from 25 December 2018, the HTS voice is from 25 December 2012, and the page has no newer dated items. I did not find a last-commit date, so I cannot confirm current maintenance.
brief.caveats: The homepage says it works on Linux and gives no macOS or Windows note. The dictionary must be compiled or downloaded in one of three encodings. The Japanese demo page is in Japanese. The mailing list says you must subscribe before posting, and HTS and the HTS demo script are not supported on it. The license is Modified BSD.
quotes: Open JTalk is a Japanese text-to-speech system.
